mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign company registry or competent authority of country of origin

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory customer due diligence under FICA requires screening of all directors and UBOs against the South African Financial Intelligence Centre (FIC) lists, the UN Security Council sanctions consolidated list, and domestic terrorist designations under the Protection of Constitutional Democracy against Terrorism and Related Activities Act. OFAC SDN screening is implemented as an institutional risk control in addition to locally mandated screening. Enhanced due diligence applies to any politically exposed person (PEP), including foreign PEPs, immediate family members, and close associates.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) e-Services portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be in one or more of South Africa's 12 official languages but must be transliterated into the Roman alphabet. The name must end with the mandatory suffix '(Pty) Ltd' for a proprietary limited company. Names must not be offensive, misleading, or in conflict with existing registered names. Any name containing a foreign script or characters must be submitted in romanized form with a certified English translation.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection by the CIPC, the applicant may file a written request for reconsideration with the Companies Tribunal within 15 business days of notification. The request must set out the legal and factual grounds for review, cite the relevant sections of the Companies Act 71 of 2008 and Companies Regulations 2011, and pay the prescribed reconsideration fee. The Tribunal will issue a directive or ruling within 60 business days. Alternatively, the applicant may reserve an amended name through the CIPC e-Services portal without prejudice.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Allowed for the digital webtoon publishing industry provided the registered office address is a physical location within South Africa where legal process may be served. A post office box or digital-only address is insufficient. A virtual office service that supplies a physical street address and dedicated mail handling is acceptable, subject to the landlord's authorization and CIPC recordal.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (estimated annual probability of unannounced CIPC physical inspection is below 5% for a low-risk online content business). Inspections may be triggered by formal creditor complaints, tax delinquency, or regulatory non-compliance flags.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act No. 71 of 2008 (as amended) read with Companies Regulations, 2011; sections 12, 13, 14, 19, 66 and 69.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), an agency of the Department of Trade, Industry and Competition (the dtic).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.1) together with the Memorandum of Incorporation (MOI), Form CoR 9.2 (Registered Office) and Form CoR 9.3 (Consent to Act as Director); filed electronically through CIPC eServices.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Companies Act 2008 imposes no minimum paid-up capital for a proprietary limited company; incorporation may proceed with one share. Share subscription proceeds are payable into the company’s post-registration bank account and no statutory escrow account is prescribed.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, by the founding board of the company, as follows: 1. The valid subscription offers set out in the Memorandum of Incorporation are accepted, the subscribed shares are allotted to the founding subscribers, and share certificates shall be issued under the Companies Act 71 of 2008. 2. The registered office of the company is adopted as [registered address], South Africa; CIPC shall be notified of any future change. 3. The following persons are appointed as first directors: [director names], each accepting office in accordance with the Memorandum of Incorporation and the Companies Act. 4. The chairperson of the board is appointed, and all incorporation forms and bank account opening resolutions are authorised.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name availability search and reservation with CIPC
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC eServices portal, Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (www.cipc.co.za)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to CIPC eServices, search the proposed company name, and file Form CoR 9.1 to reserve it. The reservation is valid for 20 business days and must be renewed if the incorporation is not completed within that window.
required_dossiers: Completed Form CoR 9.1 (Application for Reservation of Name)
Certified copy of incorporator’s identity document or passport
Power of attorney if filed by a registered company formation agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CIPC queries the name for similarity or colloquial conflict, respond through eServices with a consent letter from the prior rights holder or propose an amended name and resubmit; unresolved disputes follow section 160 of the Companies Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upload the signed MOI and completed Form CoR 14.1, together with Forms CoR 9.2 and CoR 9.3. Pay the statutory CIPC filing fee electronically, then retain the automated CIPC reference number until the registration certificate is issued.
required_dossiers: Signed and initialed Memorandum of Incorporation
Form CoR 14.1 (Notice of Incorporation)
Form CoR 9.2 (Notice of Registered Office)
Form CoR 9.3 (Consents to act as first directors)
Proof of CIPC fee payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a validation query or rejection notice is issued, correct the specified MOI provisions or forms and reply within the eServices prescribed period; if the MOI contains impermissible provisions, amend the MOI and refile the complete package.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: SARS income tax and employer registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) eFiling portal or SARS branch
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the incorporated company on SARS eFiling for income tax and obtain an income tax reference number. Where employees will be appointed, register as an employer for PAYE, SDL and UIF deductions; assess VAT registration obligations based on projected taxable supplies.
required_dossiers: CIPC registration certificate
Memorandum of Incorporation
Director identification documents and SARS registration forms
Registered office or business premises address proof
Company bank account details once opened
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SARS eFiling validation fails, correct the legal entity details and resubmit the verification documents; taxpayers may also visit a SARS branch to address unresolved taxpayer profile mismatches.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: UIF and Compensation Fund employer registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Employment and Labour (Unemployment Insurance Fund and Compensation Fund)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After tax registration, register the company as an employer with the UIF and complete Employers’ Compensation Fund registration for occupational injury and disease liability. Submit employee detail and remuneration schedules and request confirmation of the UIF and Compensation Fund employer codes.
required_dossiers: CIPC registration certificate
SARS employer registration number
Employee information list and certified identity documents
Remuneration schedule and company bank details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If duplicate or mismatched employer records are identified, provide CIPC and SARS reference numbers to the UIF/Compensation Fund service office and request reinstatement or issuance of distinct employer codes.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal premises zoning and building compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local municipality – Planning, Building Control and Fire Safety offices
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Verify that the registered office and webtoon production studio premises carry appropriate business zoning; submit building plans for approval if the space has not been certified, arrange fire-safety inspection, and obtain the certificate of occupancy before business operations commence.
required_dossiers: Lease agreement or title deed
Municipal zoning certificate
Approved building plans and any prior certificate of occupancy
Fire equipment inspection report
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where building control issues a non-compliance notice, engage a registered architect or structural engineer to remedy deviations and obtain re-inspection; appeal local municipal planning enforcement under the applicable municipal by-laws.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No manufacturing or industrial licensing board is engaged; premises and workplace authorities consist of the local municipal planning/building control department and the Department of Employment and Labour (Chief Directorate: Occupational Health and Safety).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal Certificate of Occupancy for office/creative premises and workplace compliance clearance; digital webtoon publishing is not subject to a sector-specific operating licence in South Africa.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – office-based digital publishing does not trigger listed activities under the NEMA EIA Regulations, 2014; no full EIA or environmental authorisation required unless premises include significant physical infrastructure not contemplated by standard office use.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater or point-source atmospheric emissions are generated; compliance required with municipal sewer and waste disposal by-laws and, if standby generators are installed, the atmospheric emission and noise thresholds of the National Environmental Management: Air Quality Act 39 of 2004.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate from the local municipal fire department, structural inspection and certificate of occupancy from municipal building control, and an occupational health and safety workplace clearance under the Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) - unitary national authority; primary portals: SARS eFiling (https://www.sars.gov.za / https://efiling.sars.gov.za) for income tax, VAT, PAYE, and corporate registration; SARS Customs external portal for SAD500 declarations and customs client registration; CIPC (Companies and Intellectual Property Commission) handles incorporation with automatic data exchange to SARS.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) Incorporate a Proprietary Limited company with CIPC under the Companies Act 71 of 2008; 2) SARS automatically issues the corporate income tax reference number through the integrated CIPC-SARS e-records feed; confirm issuance on eFiling under the taxpayer profile; 3) Appoint a public officer (Tax Administration Act s246) within one month of incorporation and submit the appointment via eFiling; 4) Register for VAT (VAT101 form) on eFiling once taxable turnover exceeds or is reasonably expected to exceed ZAR 1,000,000 in any 12-month period (voluntary registration from ZAR 50,000); 5) If employees are hired, register for PAYE/UIF/SDL; 6) For a non-resident entity without local incorporation, register as an external company with CIPC and as a non-resident company with SARS for CIT/VAT/PAYE based on South African source income or permanent establishment exposure under the applicable DTA.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; (Pty) Ltd is a separate legal taxpayer subject to corporate income tax at the standard rate of 27%; distributions are subject to 20% Dividends Tax at shareholder level. Territorial scope: South African resident companies are taxed on worldwide income; non-resident companies are taxed only on South African-source income attributable to a permanent establishment. No general tax-exempt zone applies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No IRS-style check-the-box election exists under South African law. Available statutory classifications and elections: (a) Headquarter Company election (s9I Income Tax Act) for foreign-controlled South African companies meeting substance requirements, providing CFC and dividend participation relief; (b) Small Business Corporation election (s12E) for qualifying close-held companies with annual turnover not exceeding ZAR 20 million; (c) Micro Business turnover tax election (Sixth Schedule) for qualifying companies with turnover up to ZAR 1 million; (d) VAT group registration election (s50 VAT Act) allowing VAT vendors within a group to register as a single VAT unit; (e) Voluntary VAT registration election from ZAR 50,000 turnover; (f) Hybrid mismatch rules (ss 8E, 9DA-9DE Income Tax Act) apply mandatorily as disallowance rules rather than elective provisions, with disclosure obligations for structured hybrid arrangements.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax - VAT Act 89 of 1991, administered nationally by SARS
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: ZAR 1,000,000 (compulsory registration when taxable supplies exceed or are reasonably likely to exceed ZAR 1,000,000 in any consecutive 12-month period; voluntary registration permitted from ZAR 50,000). Note: The 2025 Budget Review proposed an increase of the compulsory threshold to ZAR 1,500,000 effective 1 April 2026, subject to enactment.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: SARS has introduced a phased mandatory e-invoicing framework aligned with OECD standards: VAT vendors with annual taxable turnover exceeding ZAR 10 million must issue structured electronic tax invoices with near-real-time SARS validation through the eFiling API from 1 September 2025; vendors with turnover above ZAR 1 million are required to do so from 1 September 2026. The model requires submission of invoice metadata (UBL/XML) to SARS upon issuance and receipt of a unique transaction identifier; there is no physical fiscal stamp requirement, but only validated e-invoices constitute acceptable tax invoices for input VAT deduction. Non-compliant vendors may face blocked input VAT recovery and administrative penalties.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: s11(1)(a) of the VAT Act zero-rates goods physically exported from South Africa within the prescribed period (generally 90 days from supply) where the exporter retains prescribed documentary proof. Services: s11(2)(l) zero-rates services supplied to a non-resident recipient who is outside South Africa at the time the services are rendered, provided the services are not connected to South African land or movable property and are not supplied to a South African resident. Digital webtoon publishing and multilingual content syndication sold through Apple IAP and Google Play to foreign end-users qualify for zero-rating where the contractual chain identifies the non-resident as the recipient (whether the platform acts as principal or disclosed agent) and economic substance confirms the foreign destination of the supply. Electronic services supplied to South African residents remain taxable at 15%, requiring a clear segregation of domestic and export revenue streams.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD500 / SAD901-E) filed electronically via the SARS Customs platform - required for physical exports of goods to evidence the zero-rated supply
Bill of Lading (ocean freight) or Airway Bill (air freight) - evidencing physical movement of goods out of the SACU customs area within the applicable export period
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) or foreign exchange credit advice issued by an authorised dealer - evidencing repatriation of export proceeds into South Africa within the statutory deadline

For digital services exports: merchant-of-record agreements with Apple/Google, IP licensing and syndication contracts, customer residency logs, and payment gateway reports serve as the substantiation bundle in lieu of customs declarations
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: SARS audits export zero-rating claims on a documentary and risk-rated basis. Where substantiation is deficient or the 180-day forex repatriation deadline is missed without an approved exchange-control extension, SARS may reverse the zero-rating and assess VAT plus interest. Further consequences: additional tax up to 200% of the tax shortfall (VAT Act s60); understatement penalties graded by conduct - 25% for substantial understatement, 50% for failure to take reasonable care, 75% for no reasonable grounds, and 150% for intentional tax evasion (TAA ss222-223); criminal prosecution for fraudulent export claims with fines and/or imprisonment of up to five years (VAT Act s58; TAA s235). The vendor's registration may additionally be terminated or security demanded where a pattern of abuse is established.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB), acting through the Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv), as the national Exchange Control Authority under the Currency and Exchanges Act, 1933
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The South African rand (ZAR) is listed as a freely floating currency; current account transactions are generally convertible with documentary evidence. Capital account transactions remain subject to exchange control; non-resident direct investment is permitted without prior approval, but the subsequent disposal, repatriation, or write-off of capital must be reported through an Authorized Dealer. Profit and dividend remittances are permitted provided the company files tax clearance certificates through SARS and maintains audited/signed financial statements demonstrating distributable reserves. There is no blanket withholding impediment on dividends, but dividends are subject to South African dividends tax at the statutory rate; the practical remittance hurdle is documentary compliance rather than convertibility restriction.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: All export proceeds, including revenue from digital webtoon syndication and multilingual chapter unlocking, must be received into a South African bank account through an Authorized Dealer within 180 days from the date of export, invoice, or accrual. The full amount of foreign currency export revenue must be converted to rand immediately upon receipt unless a Foreign Currency Account has been pre-approved by FinSurv. Retention in foreign currency requires prior authorization and is only granted where the entity demonstrates a bona fide operational need. Non-compliance creates an exchange control offence and triggers administrative penalties.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Standard Bank of South Africa Limited
FirstRand Bank Limited (Rand Merchant Bank division for corporate treasury)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low regulatory feasibility. The Financial Sector Regulation Act and Banks Act, 1990 require deposit-taking and cross-border payment initiation to be performed by licensed banks or registered authorized payment service providers under SARB's National Payment System. Offshore electronic money institutions (EMIs) have no standalone statutory authorization to on-board a South African operating company or to settle ZAR-denominated flows. Non-resident EMI accounts may be used as ancillary collection venues for foreign-currency microtransactions, but must be connected to an Authorized Dealer bank in South Africa for conversion and repatriation. The entity should rely on licensed domestic commercial banks as the primary clearing spine.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No rigid statutory mandate requiring physical appearance of directors is imposed for all corporates, but the Financial Intelligence Centre Act (FICA) and banks' risk-based onboarding policies require full identification and verification. In practice, South African tier-1 banks generally require at least one executive director or an authorised signatory to complete a physical KYC interview at a designated bank branch, or before a South African Commissioner of Oaths / Notary, for non-resident shareholders. Remote acceptance may be permitted for low-risk entities after enhanced due diligence and video verification, but discretionary approval remains with the bank's compliance committee; the safe compliance baseline is physical appearance or notarized verification from a recognised foreign jurisdiction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholding and opaque beneficial ownership chain
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Register of Members, share allotments, trust deeds or corporate registers where applicable, personal identification documents of ultimate beneficial owners, source of wealth declarations, and a diagram of the ownership chain with no nominees or bearer shares.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk income source from digital platform payouts (Apple IAP / Google Play Billing)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed webtoon license/download agreements, dashboards of monthly in-platform sales by territory, platform payout statements showing gross receipts and platform fees, audience royalty statements, and a reconciled transaction accrual ledger.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transactions to or from financial action task force grey-listed jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial rationale memos, underlying contracts, SWIFT message references, proof of market entry or licensing, tax residence certificates, and appropriate economic substance documentation such as employee payroll and server hosting agreements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Intra-group or shareholder loan advances and rapid re-clearing of funds
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Formal loan agreements, board resolutions authorizing the borrowing, detailed repayment schedules, transfer pricing documentation under Section 31 of the Income Tax Act, and full source-of-funds evidence for each inward transfer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Potential nexus to intellectual property royalty leakage or tax evasion
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Arm's-length licensing agreement, market comparables royalty rate study, SARS tax clearance status, evidence of BOIP registration of copyright, and detailed allocation of revenue to South African vs deemed foreign sources.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Non-resident shareholders shall inject equity capital exclusively through an Authorized Dealer under exchange-control-compliant wire transfer protocols. Each incoming SWIFT MT103 must include the legal entity name, company registration number, and an instruction referencing 'non-resident direct equity subscription'. The Authorized Dealer will allocate the appropriate balance-of-payments category (direct investment – equity capital) and require a completed inward transfer notification form, source-of-funds evidence, a board allotment resolution, and a copy of the proposed share register. Funds for share subscription must be credited to a Capital Escrow Account and cannot be commingled with working capital until the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) share issuance particulars are updated. The Authorized Dealer is required to maintain a record of the underlying foreign liability for the South African Reserve Bank's quarterly reporting.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: All outbound trade settlements—including overseas syndication partner royalties, commissioned translation costs, platform settlement charges, and content distribution fees—shall be executed via SWIFT gpi MT103 messages with full OCR/FX reference, or by Commercial Letter of Credit under UCP600 for high-value deliverable contracts. Domestic transactions clear through the South African Multiple Option Settlement (SAMOS) system, while regional rand settlements for Southern African Development Community (SADC) counterparties may use the SADC-RTGS real-time gross settlement rail. Every outward transfer must reference an underlying contract and be tagged with the applicable exchange-control purpose; bank-issued foreign currency purchase for these disbursements requires a completed Foreign Exchange Application and, for amounts exceeding approved thresholds, SARS tax clearance.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outward forwards (forward exchange contracts) for committed trade payables/receivables
Inward and outward rolling hedge programmes with commission or netting features applicable to repeat webtoon licensing revenues
Cross-currency swaps covering non-deliverable revenue streams while maintaining underlying exposure
Currency options with premium paid out of operating cash to cap depreciation risk on foreign-currency royalty receipts
Combination forwards (managed forwards) aligned to projected platform payout cycles

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: CIPC Annual Return (AR) - Companies Act 71 of 2008, section 33(1)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 business days after the anniversary of the date of incorporation (anniversary month cycle)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers CIPC penalty assessment; failure to file for two consecutive years commences administrative deregistration (strike-off); directors face disqualification and personal liability; reinstatement within 2 years requires CIPC restoration filing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership Confirmation (Beneficial Ownership Register submitted with Annual Return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, simultaneously with the Annual Return; additionally, within 10 business days after any change in beneficial ownership or shareholding transfer
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance under the General Laws (Anti-Money Laundering and Combating Terrorist Financing) Amendment Act 2022 exposes the company and directors to administrative penalties and criminal prosecution; CIPC may reject the Annual Return and flag the company for regulatory intervention.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements (AFS) - preparation, Board approval, shareholder presentation, and conditional filing with CIPC
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders in general meeting; CIPC filing required only where a statutory audit is compulsory (Public Interest Score of 100 or more)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: AFS must be prepared and presented within 6 months after financial year end; if audited, AFS must be filed with CIPC within 30 business days after Board approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Contravention of sections 30 and 33 of the Companies Act; CIPC may issue Compliance Notices and refer for fines up to ZAR 1,000,000; directors may be held personally liable for failure to produce statutory AFS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (ITR14) and semiannual provisional returns (IRP6)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: ITR14 due within 12 months after financial year end; IRP6 provisional returns due at the 6th and 12th month of the financial year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: SARS may raise an estimated assessment; late payment attracts prescribed interest and a 10% late-payment penalty; understatement penalties up to 200% of the underpaid tax apply for substantial understatements.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent statutory audit is compulsory when the company's Public Interest Score (PI Score) reaches 100 or more in the relevant financial year; PI Score of 50-99 mandates an independent review; PI Score below 50 requires only AFS compilation. A low-risk webtoon publishing (Pty) Ltd with turnover below ZAR 10 million and fewer than 10 employees ordinarily has a PI Score below 50 and no compulsory external audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS or IFRS for SMEs (South African GAAP) as prescribed by the Companies Regulations 2011, regulation 27; IFRS is mandatory for public companies and for companies with a PI Score of 350 or above.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: At each annual return cycle, the company must validate the Beneficial Ownership Register and confirm to CIPC all direct and indirect beneficial owners, including percentage entitlements and control mechanisms; any shareholding transfer or new beneficial owner must be entered in the Register and filed with CIPC within 10 business days of the change; the annual confirmation is accepted only when the CIPC beneficial ownership record matches the actual shareholding.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 150 - 650 (ZAR 3,000 - 12,000) per annum for local registered office and annual company secretarial administration
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,000 - 4,000 (ZAR 18,500 - 74,000) per annum for a statutory audit; USD 400 - 900 (ZAR 7,400 - 16,600) per annum for an independent review

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27.0% (years of assessment ending on or after 31 March 2023)
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Indefinite (carried forward without statutory time limit; s.20A of the Income Tax Act requires that the company must carry on a trade in the relevant year to set off the assessed loss).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: ITR14 – Company Income Tax Return, filed electronically via SARS eFiling
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 12 months after the end of the company's financial year (the specific due date is set by SARS's notice of assessment / eFiling 'return issued' letter); provisional taxpayers additionally file IRP6 returns.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company registration number, SARS tax reference number, financial year-end date, case status.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Not applicable – the entity is a South African tax resident (incorporated in ZA). Foreign shareholder particulars captured on the shareholder registers, not on this return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All worldwide gross receipts and accruals, including Apple IAP and Google Play Billing proceeds (gross, before 15%-30% app-store commission), advertising and syndication/sub-licensing income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign-source income must be included; app-store remittances net of commission are not gross income – but the full consumer-facing gross amount is taxable income with the commission deductible. Translate foreign currency at the SARS ruling spot rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign dividends and other exempt receipts (s.10(1)(k), s.10B etc.) if strict requirements are met.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only where the foreign dividend/collection qualifies; attach the Schedule recognising withholding tax borne.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section H – Deductions and special allowances
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: App-store platform commissions, content licensing fees, artist/development staff costs, Section 11D R&D super-deduction, ancillary bank charges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border royalty and service payments to related parties require arm's-length substantiation and s.31 TP documentation; otherwise the deduction is disallowed. A s.23(k) limitation applies to non-deductible royalties paid to non-residents who are not subject to SA normal tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Assessed loss brought forward and current-year loss.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses may be set off indefinitely only if the company carries on a trade in that year; a change in shareholding/control within 3 years followed by trade cessation forfeits the loss (s.20A).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section L – Taxable income and rate
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income computed; apply 27% headline rate or SBC sliding scale.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credits (s.6quat) allowed for WHT proved on foreign-source income; credits are capped to the SA tax on that income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: IRP6 payments (first, second and any voluntary third) offset against the final normal tax liability.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The non-resident parent cannot offset its own foreign payments against the SA company's liability; the SA entity must settle its tax.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late/non-submission: administrative non-compliance penalty of ZAR 250 to ZAR 16,000 per month (capped at 35 months) depending on turnover; 10% late-payment penalty plus interest at the prescribed rate (SARB repo rate + 3.5%) on unpaid tax; estimated assessment and criminal prosecution (fine or imprisonment up to 5 years) for persistent default.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IRP6 – Provisional Tax Return (for provisional taxpayers), via SARS eFiling
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Semi-annual (two compulsory estimates plus optional third top-up)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: First half-year estimate: due within 6 months of the start of the year of assessment. Second estimate: due on the last business day of the year of assessment. Voluntary third payment (companies): due within 6 months of year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Estimate of current-year chargeable income (including CGT).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Estimate must be realistic; repeated low estimates trigger the underestimation penalty.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prior-year final assessed taxable income used as a floor for the under-estimation rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The basic amount is determined on the ZA company's own return, not the parent's.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: 50% (first payment) and 100% (second) of total estimated normal tax, net of employees' tax and foreign tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The company cannot defer second-payment liability by relying on the foreign parent's remittance schedule; funds must be retained.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Under-estimation penalty of 20% of the shortfall between the final assessment and the provisional amounts paid (TAA s.163) where the estimate is below the basic amount or less than 80% of actual taxable income; prescribed-rate interest compounded daily from the original due date.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% on dividends paid by a ZA-resident company (Dividend Tax, s.64E Income Tax Act), payable by the beneficial owner but withheld by the company as agent within 30 days of the dividend becoming payable.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply a reduced DTA rate (typically 5% on ≥10% shareholding, 10%-15% otherwise): (1) obtain a current Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the shareholder's tax authority; (2) complete the applicable SARS dividend withholding declaration confirming beneficial ownership and the treaty article; (3) submit the TRC and declaration to the ZA payer before payment so the reduced rate is applied at source; (4) retain documents for 5 years; (5) if WHT was over-deducted, the non-resident must file a refund application within 3 years. Treaty benefits are refused where the main purpose is treaty shopping (MLI Principal Purpose Test).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 15% statutory WHT, commonly reduced to 10% (range 0%-12%) under DTAs (e.g., SA-UK and SA-US at 10%-12%); interest: 15% statutory WHT, generally reduced to 10% or 0% under DTAs. Payments for contracted webtoon/trademark IP licenses and intercompany loans must be reported on the relevant SARS WHT declarations and paid to SARS monthly.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Contemporaneous Local File and Master File are required where cross-border related-party transactions exceed ZAR 5 million (goods) or ZAR 1 million (services, intangibles, financing) per the SARS TP Guide 2023; Country-by-Country Report is mandatory for groups with consolidated turnover of at least ZAR 10 billion.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP – Comparable Uncontrolled Price (preferred for IP licensing and digital content)
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Not a standalone ESR regime as in the UAE. Substance is enforced through the place-of-effective-management (POEM) residence test, the CFC attribution rules (s.9D), GAAR (s.80A-80L), and the DTA Principal Purpose Test. The company must maintain employees, premises, strategic decision-making, and IP-development substance in South Africa to avoid re-characterisation as a shell conduit.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of Apple IAP / Google Play consumer receipts; crediting app-store net payments instead of gross revenue; fake content-cost invoices from a related BVI/Cayman entity; keeping shadow financial records.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Understatement penalty up to 150% of the tax shortfall for intentional evasion (TAA s.223); interest accrual; criminal indictment – fine up to double the evaded tax and/or imprisonment up to 5 years (TAA s.235); SARS may issue an estimated assessment under s.95.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly sign false returns are criminally liable; personal liability for the company's unpaid withholding taxes under s.179 TAA; travel bans and asset import/export prohibitions under s.194 TAA; restraint orders under POCA.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Za (Pty) Ltd is a mailbox entity: no staff in ZA except a nominee director, comic IP legally owned in a low-tax jurisdiction, 90% of revenue remitted abroad as royalties, no board meetings, operational control (Google/Apple accounts, payments, treasury) exercised outside ZA.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: POEM determination shifts residence/taxation outside or inside ZA; s.31 transfer-pricing adjustment of the royalty outflow; s.23(k) deduction denial; GAAR (s.80A-80L) can void the entire arrangement; TP penalty and a 100%-150% understatement penalty; DTA relief denied under the PPT.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing the corporate veil: restitution of the full adjusted tax plus penalties from personal estate; directors may be jointly liable under s.179 TAA; criminal sanctions for fraudulent preference of foreign shareholders over SARS claims; travel bans pending payment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Declaring dividends to a non-resident without withholding 20% (or treaty rate); paying related-party license fees or interest without deducting 15% WHT; failing to file WHT declarations within 30 days or to obtain TRCs before applying DTA rates.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The payer company is statutorily liable for the full un-withheld amount (s.64J), plus a 10% late-payment penalty and prescribed interest; monthly administrative non-compliance penalties for unfiled declarations; understatement penalties up to 150% where the failure was deliberate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable for un-withheld dividends tax (s.64J(3) read with s.179 TAA); criminal prosecution for failure to perform a statutory obligation; disqualification proceedings under the Companies Act.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Financial Intelligence Centre Act (FICA) & Exchange Control
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Routing of consumer payments through foreign PSPs to disguise beneficial ownership; failing to submit Suspicious Transaction Reports where the webtoon billing operation functions as a payment-accepting business; unauthorised externalisation of funds abroad without SARB/Authorised Dealer approval; unlawful refund laundering via in-app coin structures.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: FICA s.50-51: fines up to ZAR 10 million per offence and/or imprisonment up to 15 years; POCA money-laundering: fine up to ZAR 100 million and/or imprisonment up to 30 years; Exchange Control Regulations contraventions: administrative penalties of up to ZAR 5,000 per day plus forfeiture of the foreign currency.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Criminal liability of directors and any appointed Money Laundering Control Officer; restraint and forfeiture of personal assets; travel bans and extradition exposure; prohibition from serving as directors of any company.
